stable_traits: trains finger strength on a hangboard

dialogue.content: What warm-up do you recommend before any board session?
Start with open-hand dead hangs at bodyweight, then easy pull-ups, then short edge touches. Stop if anything feels pinchy in a finger joint.
I tweaked a finger pulley last season. It feels mostly okay now, but I am still avoiding peak one-arm edge efforts and sticking to easier open-hand work.
That is a sensible guardrail. Easier open-hand loading while you stay away from peak one-arm edge efforts reduces re-injury risk.
Should I ice after every session or only when something feels irritated?
Only when something feels irritated. Routine icing after normal sessions is usually unnecessary.
Gyms love challenge signups. How do I evaluate whether a signup is useful training or just marketing?
Check whether the challenge signup matches your current limits. If it pushes a quality you are deliberately avoiding, it is marketing, not training.
Any non-board forearm work that will not spike tendon load?
Rice-bucket rotations and light wrist curls with high control are usually gentler than dense edge work.
A friend said the gym challenge signup this month is amazing. I am on the fence about whether I should join.
Filter any challenge signup against what you already decided to protect. Hype alone is not a reason to join.
The climbing gym is pushing a max-hang challenge signup this month. Should I join?

query: The climbing gym is pushing a max-hang challenge signup this month. Should I join?
gold_answer: No. After a prior finger pulley strain you are still avoiding peak one-arm edge efforts. A max-hang challenge signup is the same kind of peak loading, so skip it for now.
